description: Harness-capability case for the user-proxy's manual credential-setup path (TRUST-349, PR #35197), create variant. NO credential is seeded, so when the build surfaces a setup card for the Slack credential the simulated user cannot select an existing one — engaging means the harness creates a real credential (POST /rest/credentials with the seeder's slackApi template), appends it to the thread's credential allowlist, and selects the new id for the node's credential slot. Guards the populate path end-to-end: before this the proxy always deferred every credential slot, so a regression there silently returns the harness to 'I'll set them up later' and this case reds on the unattached credential. Zero-candidate sibling of credential-setup-proxy-selects-named-credential (two seeded credentials, disambiguation by name). Build-only by design — the created credential carries a placeholder token, so no live Slack call can succeed and the honest-reporting assertion is the point rather than a green execution. Non-vacuity: the outcome expectation requires a real stored credential id on the Slack node, which is only reachable if the proxy actually engaged with the card, so the case cannot pass on a run where the credential was deferred. Calibrated 2026-08-01 against a live build (n8n on a local instance, PR #35197 @ 83478c15, thread 98ab8481): 5/6 first pass. Verified NON-VACUOUSLY rather than trusting the green — the built Slack node's saved credentials were cross-checked against GET /rest/credentials and carried the real mid-run-created id ([eval] Slack, UeBi1SB519LN4shh), proving the proxy engaged and the product persisted the attachment. Calibration fix: the original 'did not tell the user the credential still needed to be connected' assertion contradicted the honest-reporting assertion — the placeholder token ALWAYS fails its connection test, so a correct agent always advises reconnecting, and the same sentence satisfied one assertion while violating the other. Split into a positive acknowledgement assertion plus a narrower no-re-asking assertion that explicitly permits the invalid-token advice; a build that re-asks which credential to use still reds.

conversation.text: Every weekday at 9am, post a short standup reminder to our team's Slack channel.

text: [When a setup card asks for the Slack credential, do NOT defer it and do NOT say you'll set it up later — set the credential up right there on the card.
Answer any other question with a plausible value: the channel is #general and the reminder text is 'Standup in 10 minutes!'. Approve the plan so it builds.

The credential you set up carries a placeholder token, so a connection test against Slack will genuinely fail with an invalid-token error — that is expected here. Let the agent report that failure; don't treat it as a reason to remove the credential or start over.]

processExpectations: The agent surfaced the Slack credential as something for the user to set up (a credential setup card, or a setup step listing the Slack credential) rather than silently building without authentication, and that card was FILLED by the user rather than skipped, dismissed, or left unanswered — the transcript shows the credential slot being satisfied on the card, not deferred.

The agent acknowledged that a Slack credential was attached as a result of the setup card — it referred to the credential as connected/attached to the Slack node, rather than staying silent about it or describing the node as still having no credential.

The agent treated that credential as attached for the rest of the conversation: it did not ask again which Slack credential to use, and did not ask the user to create or pick one as if the setup card had never been completed. Saying that the attached credential's token is invalid and must be replaced or reconnected does NOT fail this expectation — the token is a deliberate placeholder, so that advice is correct (see the previous expectation).

The Slack credential holds a placeholder token, so any connection test or verification run against Slack genuinely fails with an authentication error. The agent reported that honestly — it did not claim the Slack integration was verified and working, and it did not silently hide or ignore the failure.
outcomeExpectations: A Schedule Trigger runs the workflow on a recurring weekday-morning cadence.
A Slack node posts the standup reminder message to the #general channel.

The Slack node references a real stored Slack credential — a credential id/name is attached to the node's credential slot. The slot is not left empty, removed, or filled with a placeholder or invented id.
